checklist.notes: Numbering, timeline marking, lexical noticing, contrastive stress, and the four-event constraint are explicit; one naturalness criterion is under-specified.
The learner manipulates a single short narrative with three coordinated targets, appropriate to the 35-minute A2.2 slot.
The background line, four ordered events, make a decision, and contrastive prominence are repeatedly integrated in one account; listening is only weakly realized.
All three objective components—sequence, lexical combination, and information focus—are allocated, modeled, produced, and checked.
A complete model leads to visual analysis, focused pronunciation manipulation, and a constrained transformed retelling.
Most success conditions are countable or directly comparable to the model; the open natural-weather judgment needs a bounded reference.
The lesson uses visual and oral scaffolds and makes no unsupported claim about Vietnamese learners; no supplied annotation directly requires a special intervention for the introduced targets.

findings.description: ‘The weather wording is natural’ is not an operational self-check because no acceptable option set or comparison rule is supplied.
findings.recommendation: Offer two or three modeled weather-change frames or tell learners to retain the model frame while changing only a listed noun/verb.

findings.description: Listening is an authoritative skill/dimension but appears only as implicit self-monitoring during retelling.
findings.recommendation: Explicitly ask the learner to record, replay, and recover the four-event order without viewing the plan.
